title: Example content pack
description: A small valid pack that shows every field. It adds a new category, two concepts, two questions, one scenario, two multiple-choice questions and a two-stage process.

concepts.name: Interest coverage
concepts.summary: EBIT (or EBITDA) divided by interest expense. Shows how comfortably a company can pay the interest on its debt.

concepts.name: Net leverage
concepts.summary: Net debt divided by EBITDA. A standard measure of how heavily a company is borrowed relative to its earnings.

questions.title: Interest coverage ratio
questions.prompt: What does the interest coverage ratio tell you, and how is it calculated?
answer: Interest coverage measures how many times a company's operating earnings can pay its interest expense. A higher ratio means more room before earnings fall short of interest payments.
It is usually EBIT divided by interest expense. EBITDA is used as well, which gives a higher and more generous ratio because it ignores depreciation and amortisation.

questions.title: Why lenders use net leverage
questions.prompt: Why do lenders look at net debt to EBITDA?
answer: It compares what a company owes, after counting the cash it could use to repay debt, with the earnings that service the debt. It is a quick way to judge how many years of EBITDA it would take to repay borrowings.
Lenders set limits on it in loan agreements (covenants), and acquirers use it to size how much debt a deal can carry.

scenarios.title: Repaying debt with cash
scenarios.prompt: A company repays $50m of debt using $50m of its cash. What happens to its net leverage?
answer: Before: net debt is $500m − $100m = $400m, so net leverage is $400m ÷ $125m = 3.2x.
After: debt falls to $450m and cash falls to $50m, so net debt is still $400m and net leverage is still 3.2x.
Repaying debt with cash lowers gross debt but leaves net debt unchanged, so net leverage does not move.

multipleChoice.title: Calculating interest coverage
multipleChoice.prompt: A company has EBIT of $60m and interest expense of $40m. What is its interest coverage ratio?
explanation: Interest coverage is EBIT divided by interest expense, so $60m ÷ $40m = 1.5x.
The inverse, 0.67x, would be interest divided by EBIT.

multipleChoice.title: Calculating net leverage
multipleChoice.prompt: A company has $300m of debt, $100m of cash and $100m of EBITDA. What is its net leverage?
explanation: Net debt is $300m − $100m = $200m, so net leverage is $200m ÷ $100m = 2.0x.
3.0x would be gross leverage, which ignores the cash.
